statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the following holds. A row/column-swap sequence is a finite sequence of moves, each move swapping two distinct rows or two distinct columns. If some row/column-swap sequence transforms board into a chessboard, meaning no two 4-directionally adjacent entries are equal, then r is the minimum length of such a sequence. If no such sequence exists, then r = -1. Equivalently: r = -1 exactly when no row/column-swap sequence reaches a chessboard; otherwise r >= 0 and there is a sequence of exactly r swaps reaching a chessboard, but no sequence of fewer than r swaps does so.
preconditions: Let n = len(board). Assume 2 <= n <= 30, every row board[i] has length n, and every entry board[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: For every such input board, the function returns a result r, i.e. the Lean Result is a successful value and is not a failure, panic, out-of-bounds access, or arithmetic overflow.
preconditions: Let n = len(board). Assume 2 <= n <= 30, every row board[i] has length n, and every entry board[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, either r = -1, or 0 <= r <= 2*n - 2.
preconditions: Let n = len(board). Assume 2 <= n <= 30, every row board[i] has length n, and every entry board[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if board itself is already a chessboard: for all 0 <= i < n-1 and 0 <= j < n, board[i][j] != board[i+1][j], and for all 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n-1, board[i][j] != board[i][j+1].
preconditions: Let n = len(board). Assume 2 <= n <= 30, every row board[i] has length n, and every entry board[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, the total number ones = #{ (i,j) : 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, board[i][j] = 1 } satisfies |2*ones - n*n| <= 1. Equivalently, ones is floor(n*n/2) or ceil(n*n/2).
preconditions: Let n = len(board). Assume 2 <= n <= 30, every row board[i] has length n, and every entry board[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, every row is equal either to row 0 or to the bitwise complement of row 0: for every i with 0 <= i < n, either (for all j with 0 <= j < n, board[i][j] = board[0][j]) or (for all j with 0 <= j < n, board[i][j] = 1 - board[0][j]).
preconditions: Let n = len(board). Assume 2 <= n <= 30, every row board[i] has length n, and every entry board[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, every column is equal either to column 0 or to the bitwise complement of column 0: for every j with 0 <= j < n, either (for all i with 0 <= i < n, board[i][j] = board[i][0]) or (for all i with 0 <= i < n, board[i][j] = 1 - board[i][0]).
preconditions: Let n = len(board). Assume 2 <= n <= 30, every row board[i] has length n, and every entry board[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, let A be the number of rows i such that board[i][j] = board[0][j] for every j, and let B be the number of rows i such that board[i][j] = 1 - board[0][j] for every j. Then |A - B| <= 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(board). Assume 2 <= n <= 30, every row board[i] has length n, and every entry board[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, let C be the number of columns j such that board[i][j] = board[i][0] for every i, and let D be the number of columns j such that board[i][j] = 1 - board[i][0] for every i. Then |C - D| <= 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(board). Assume 2 <= n <= 30, every row board[i] has length n, and every entry board[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = -1 if and only if at least one of the following holds: (a) there is a row i that is neither equal to row 0 nor equal to the bitwise complement of row 0; (b) there is a column j that is neither equal to column 0 nor equal to the bitwise complement of column 0; (c) letting A be the number of rows equal to row 0 and B the number of rows equal to the complement of row 0, we have |A - B| > 1; (d) letting C be the number of columns equal to column 0 and D the number of columns equal to the complement of column 0, we have |C - D| > 1. Equivalently, r >= 0 if and only if all rows are of the two allowed row types, all columns are of the two allowed column types, and both pairs of type counts are balanced with difference at most one.
preconditions: Let n = len(board). Assume 2 <= n <= 30, every row board[i] has length n, and every entry board[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Let r be the result returned for board and let rT be the result returned for boardT. Then r = rT. In particular, both are -1, or both are nonnegative and equal.
preconditions: Let n = len(board). Assume 2 <= n <= 30, every row board[i] has length n, and every entry board[i][j] is either 0 or 1. Let boardT be the transpose, boardT[i][j] = board[j][i].

statement: Let r be the result returned for board and let rC be the result returned for boardC. Then r = rC.
preconditions: Let n = len(board). Assume 2 <= n <= 30, every row board[i] has length n, and every entry board[i][j] is either 0 or 1. Let boardC be obtained by replacing every entry x with 1 - x.

statement: Let r be the result returned for board and let r2 be the result returned for board2. Then either both r and r2 are -1, or both are nonnegative and |r - r2| <= 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(board). Assume 2 <= n <= 30, every row board[i] has length n, and every entry board[i][j] is either 0 or 1. Let board2 be obtained from board by swapping two distinct rows or by swapping two distinct columns.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if board is a chessboard, and r = -1 if board is not a chessboard. Thus for n = 2 no positive move count is ever returned.
preconditions: Let n = len(board). Assume n = 2, every row board[i] has length 2, and every entry board[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, there exist a bit c in {0,1}, a permutation sigma of {0,...,n-1}, and a permutation tau of {0,...,n-1} such that for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, board[sigma(i)][tau(j)] = c XOR ((i+j) mod 2). Here XOR is on bits 0 and 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(board). Assume 2 <= n <= 30, every row board[i] has length n, and every entry board[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, let n = len(board). Define t_i = 0 if row i equals row 0 and t_i = 1 if row i is the bitwise complement of row 0; define u_j = 0 if column j equals column 0 and u_j = 1 if column j is the bitwise complement of column 0. For a bit p in {0,1}, let rowMismatch(p) = #{ i : 0 <= i < n and t_i != (p XOR (i mod 2)) }; call p row-admissible if #{ i : p XOR (i mod 2) = 1 } = #{ i : t_i = 1 }. Define colMismatch(q) and q col-admissible analogously using u. Then r = ( min_{p row-admissible} rowMismatch(p) + min_{q col-admissible} colMismatch(q) ) / 2.
preconditions: Let n = len(board). Assume 2 <= n <= 30, every row board[i] has length n, and every entry board[i][j] is either 0 or 1.
